references.text: The introduction of the Garden of Eden, where God plants the garden and later places Adam.
The Lord God sends Adam out of the Garden of Eden, in contrast to his original placement there to work it and keep it.
The cultural mandate to subdue the earth and rule over the animals is closely linked to Adam's mission to cultivate and keep the garden.
The Levites' service in the tabernacle uses the same Hebrew words (עבד and שׁמר) as Adam's mission in the garden, linking the garden to the sanctuary.
The Levites' task of keeping watch (שׁמר) over the sanctuary mirrors Adam's calling to guard the Garden of Eden.
The verses form a theological contrast: 2:15 gives the mission to cultivate and keep the garden, while 3:23 shows how this mission continues, though changed, on the earth after the fall.
A clear contrast: In 2:15 humanity was given the task of guarding the garden, but in 3:24 God takes back this role and sets cherubim to guard the way.
2:9 describes the contents of the garden (the tree of life, the tree of knowledge) which humanity is commissioned to guard in 2:15; the verses are inseparable in the narrative.
